Diagnosis.submission:
Root cause: No root cause is established by this board. Span-derived metrics do not exist for nginx-web-server or compose-post-service in either the onset or baseline window because neither emits traces that become metrics [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_00357570b0e6], which makes the empty Tempo result [tr_ce237924350e] the expected baseline for an uninstrumented service rather than a symptom of silence. Both Loki queries used guessed pod-name regexes that were never validated and returned empty results carrying a truncation flag [tr_c626ef4ef205][tr_4b6926841b8a], so that silence cannot be read as the service writing nothing. The only positive evidence is a three-second burst by platform-automation about six minutes before the 07:09:07 alert in which the nginx workload container, the nginx-thrift ConfigMap and the nginx-thrift Service were all created for the first time [tr_1808ab6d2147] - a bootstrap sequence, not a regression from a healthy baseline. That tells us nginx began serving against never-exercised routing config; it does not name what is failing now.
Faulty component: nginx-web-server
Fault type: unknown
Confidence: low

Evidence:
- Only three changes are recorded for nginx-web-server across the full 24-hour window, and all three cluster within about three seconds of each other roughly six minutes before onset. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- All three changes are first-time creations rather than modifications: a workload container created for the first time, plus a ConfigMap and a Service both newly created for the nginx-thrift upstream. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- Every change was made by the same non-human actor, platform-automation, indicating an automated provisioning or bootstrap sequence rather than an operator-initiated edit. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- The upstream routing surface (Service nginx-thrift) and the upstream config (ConfigMap nginx-thrift) came into existence at the same instant as the workload, so the service began serving against freshly created, never-previously-exercised routing config. (found, from change_history on nginx-web-server)
- A config edit or regression to an existing, previously healthy nginx upstream configuration caused the incident. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The ConfigMap and Service are recorded as created, not updated, and no prior version exists in the window — there was no established baseline config to regress from.)
- A gradual or staged rollout drifted the service into a bad state over the hours preceding onset. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The window spans a full day and contains no changes at all until a single three-second burst six minutes before onset; there is no multi-step or progressive rollout to blame.)
- A human operator made a manual hotfix, routing tweak, or emergency config push shortly before the incident. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: All three recorded changes are attributed to platform-automation, with no human actor present in the change set.)
- A routing change redirected traffic away from a healthy upstream to a broken one. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The nginx-thrift Service was created, not reconfigured or repointed, so no pre-existing traffic path was altered.)
- The container was restarted, rescheduled, or redeployed from a prior revision. (ruled_out, from change_history on nginx-web-server; why: The workload is explicitly logged as first created, ruling out a restart or replacement of an earlier running instance within this window.)
- The error-ratio metric query for nginx-web-server returned no data at all across both the incident window and its preceding baseline window; the backing store holds no span-derived metrics for this service because it does not emit traces that become metrics. (found, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server)
- No error-status breakdown (5xx vs 4xx), no request rate, and no upstream latency figures are obtainable for nginx-web-server from this metrics source, so the onset question remains unanswered by this evidence. (found, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server)
- The empty result means nginx-web-server served zero errors during the window, i.e. the proxy tier is clean. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: The result carries an explicit query-failure condition stating the data is unavailable rather than zero, so absence here is instrument coverage, not a healthy signal. No conclusion about nginx error volume can be drawn either way.)
- Span-derived metrics in this Prometheus are a viable route to characterise nginx-web-server traffic, and a retry or wider window would return the breakdown. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: The failure is structural — the service emits no traces, so no span metrics exist for it in any window. Re-querying this template will keep returning nothing; nginx request rate, status mix and upstream latency must come from access logs or an nginx exporter instead.)
- The gap is specific to the incident window, suggesting a collector outage or scrape interruption coinciding with onset. (ruled_out, from metric_baseline on nginx-web-server; why: The baseline window immediately before onset is equally empty, so there is no transition from data to no-data at onset and nothing points to a collection failure triggered by the incident.)
- A trace query for nginx-web-server across the full onset window returned nothing at all — not a single trace, not even a root span that starts and immediately fails. (found, from trace_query on nginx-web-server)
- Because no spans exist, the question of which hop carries ERROR status or terminates cannot be answered from trace data: there are no nginx-web-server spans and therefore no child spans toward nginx-thrift, compose-post, home-timeline, or user-timeline to inspect. (found, from trace_query on nginx-web-server)
- The absence is total rather than partial, which points at one of two whole-path conditions: either no requests were admitted/served by nginx-web-server in this window, or the tracing path itself (instrumentation, agent, or collector export to Tempo) stopped producing data for this service. (found, from trace_query on nginx-web-server)
- Requests are reaching an upstream and failing there, with a specific downstream service (compose-post, home-timeline, or user-timeline) marked ERROR as the culprit hop. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: No spans exist for nginx-web-server or any of its children in the window, so no upstream hop can be identified as carrying ERROR status. Any claim of a specific failing hop has no trace support.)
- The failure is a partial or intermittent degradation — some traces succeed end-to-end while a fraction error out at one upstream. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: A partial failure would still leave successful traces in the window. The result is completely empty, which is inconsistent with a mixed success/failure pattern.)
- Requests enter nginx-web-server and terminate at the nginx-thrift boundary (e.g. upstream connection refused), visible as a truncated trace. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: Truncated traces would still show the nginx-web-server root span and its failed outbound attempt. No root spans exist at all, so termination cannot be localized to that boundary.)
- The trace window was simply misaligned and traces exist just outside it. (ruled_out, from trace_query on nginx-web-server; why: The query covered the full ~30-minute onset window and returned empty across its entirety, not a sparse edge region.)
- A Loki query scoped to the social-network namespace and a pod-name pattern intended to match the nginx frontend returned zero log lines across the full ~30-minute window spanning onset, so no error lines and no upstream path or host can be named from this evidence. (found, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The absence is total rather than selective: not merely no error-level lines, but no lines at all, which is consistent either with the pod selector failing to match any running pod or with no logs being ingested from this workload during the window. (found, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The result is flagged truncated despite being empty, so the emptiness should be treated as a property of the matched stream set rather than a confirmed exhaustive scan. (found, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- nginx logged upstream connection failures or timeouts naming a specific backend host/port that would identify the failing downstream dependency (ruled_out, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; why: No lines of any level were returned for the nginx stream over the onset window, so there is no logged upstream identifier available from this source; any upstream attribution must come from traces or service-mesh telemetry instead.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- nginx itself was the origin of the incident, surfacing config-reload errors, worker crashes, or 5xx generation in its own logs (ruled_out, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; why: An nginx-originated fault of that kind would normally leave error-log entries in this window; none exist, which removes log-based support for nginx as the originating component.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The investigation can proceed by reading nginx access/error logs to correlate request paths with onset (ruled_out, from logql_query on nginx-web-server; why: This log stream is unusable for correlation in this window; the next step is to validate the pod label/name pattern and log shipping rather than to re-query the same selector.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"nginx-thrift-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- A Loki query for compose-post-service pods in the social-network namespace returned no matching log lines across the full 30-minute window ending at 07:09, so there is no logged evidence of connection errors, refusals, or upstream-identity failures from this service in that period. (found, from logql_query on compose-post-service; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The absence is total rather than selective — not a single line of any level or category was returned — which is itself anomalous for a request-serving component and is consistent with either the service not running/not being scheduled under the matched pod-name pattern, or its log pipeline not delivering to Loki. (found, from logql_query on compose-post-service; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- The result carries a truncation flag despite being empty, so the query's completeness cannot be fully guaranteed; a corroborating query (relaxed label selector, or pod listing) is needed before treating the silence as conclusive. (found, from logql_query on compose-post-service; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- compose-post-service logged explicit connection refusals or upstream connect errors at 07:09 that identify the failing downstream dependency (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: No log lines at all were returned for this service over the window, so no such error text exists in Loki for this selector; the downstream dependency cannot be named from compose-post-service logs.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- An upstream-identity or TLS/peer-verification error in compose-post-service is the root cause visible in its own logs (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: The query covering the incident window returned zero lines, so no identity or verification error was emitted to the log backend by this service.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- compose-post-service was healthy and logging normally, just without errors (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: Normal operation would still produce routine request or startup lines; the complete absence of any output is inconsistent with a healthy, logging service and points toward the pod being absent, renamed, crash-looping before log emission, or its log shipping being broken.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})
- Log evidence from compose-post-service can be used to timestamp the onset of the incident (ruled_out, from logql_query on compose-post-service; why: With no lines in the window there is no timestamp sequence to anchor onset; timing must come from metrics, traces, or neighbouring services.; query: {namespace="social-network",pod=~"compose-post-service-([a-z0-9]+-[a-z0-9]+|[0-9]+)"})

Reasoning:
Four of six dispatches returned nothing, and two of those nothings are explained by instrument coverage rather than by the incident [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_00357570b0e6]. Because those services emit no traces, the total absence of spans [tr_ce237924350e] is consistent with health, freeze, partition or error alike and discriminates nothing. The log silence [tr_c626ef4ef205][tr_4b6926841b8a] is similarly unusable: the specialists flagged that the selector may simply not match any running pod, and the results were marked truncated despite being empty. That leaves only the change record [tr_1808ab6d2147], which is evidence of an act, not of a mechanism - and its own specialist ruled out config regression, staged rollout, human edit, upstream repointing and restart-from-prior-revision. Naming any fault class on this basis would be classifying by the upstream act rather than by what the service is doing wrong, so the honest verdict is unknown with the investigation pointed at validating pod identity and finding a non-span signal.

Alternatives considered:
1. nginx-web-server: The freshly created nginx-thrift ConfigMap names upstreams that do not resolve, so nginx cannot route any request. (bad_config). Ranked lower because: Nothing read the ConfigMap's contents; the change record shows only that it was created. There is no prior version to revert to and no logged upstream error naming a wrong address or port.
2. nginx-web-server: The nginx process is stopped while its socket still accepts, so callers hang and the service writes nothing. (process_freeze). Ranked lower because: The silence that would support this is not probative: traces are absent because the service is uninstrumented [tr_81d3c68dcd9a], and the log emptiness rests on an unvalidated selector with a truncation flag [tr_c626ef4ef205].

Open questions:
- Do nginx-thrift and compose-post-service pods actually exist and are they Running? The Loki selectors were unvalidated regexes, so emptiness may be a label mismatch rather than a silent service.
- What do nginx access/error logs show via a relaxed selector or an nginx exporter, since span metrics are structurally unavailable for this service?
- Did the 07:02 bootstrap complete successfully - did the container reach Ready, and does the freshly created nginx-thrift ConfigMap name upstreams that actually resolve?
